corrections.source_says: Set core to no and revise eligibility.reason to remove the two-screener routing claim. Random assignment is explicit, but creativity, novelty, usefulness, and clarity are participant self-evaluations; the externally scored output measure is value stance, not creativity or between-person diversity. Under the checker brief, has_randomized_people_study is therefore false despite the randomized design. Retain criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output=not_met and context_class=none.

confirmed: Source read: the complete markdown and all 11 PDF pages, including Appendices A-D; the PDF is arXiv:2402.12814v3 dated 22 Apr 2024, with the stated title and authors (PDF p. 1; appendices pp. 10-11).

The online_rct design is correct: participants were randomly assigned a value domain and Pro, Con, or Neutral AI condition, and completed assisted and unassisted sessions in randomized order; prompts were also randomized between sessions (PDF pp. 2-3, sections 3.1-3.3).

The reported study sample is 180 Prolific participants, 60 per domain, aged 18-60; 180 responses is separately the moderator-analysis count, not an explicit post-exclusion unique-person count (PDF p. 3, section 3.1; p. 6, section 4.3).

The response downsampling and incomplete-response exclusions are correctly described in participants.who; final unique-person counts by arm are not explicitly given, so the null arm counts should remain (PDF p. 4, section 3.6).
GPT-4 was used through a custom chat interface with Pro, Con, or Neutral value prompts; participants were asked to write at least four sentences (PDF p. 3, sections 3.3-3.4).

The tasks involved practical solutions in Economics, Automation, and Hierarchy, with the listed education, healthcare, supermarket, school, community-garden, and disaster-relief prompts; the time limit was five minutes with grace time (PDF p. 10, Appendix A; p. 8, section 5.2).
The output-value scale runs from 0 (Con) to 10 (Pro); human evaluators validated these value scores rather than rating creativity (PDF p. 4, section 3.6).

The only reported string and the one-line finding match the PDF: Pro AI M=7.49, SD=2.76 versus Neutral AI M=5.51, SD=2.97; post-hoc Tukey p=.005. These are value-stance scores (PDF p. 4, section 4.1).

No qualifying output-scored creativity or between-person diversity result is reported; the creativity-related survey items are self-evaluations, so criterion 3 is not met and context_class=none is correct (PDF pp. 4-5, sections 3.5-4.2; p. 10, Appendix B).
This is one empirical experiment, not a synthesis; no study-pooling counts, pooled estimates, or standardizing intervals need to be recorded (PDF pp. 2-7, sections 3-4).

The included appendices contain brainstorming prompts, self-evaluation items, moderator regressions with standard errors, and an example conversation with the participant's final response, as the form states (PDF pp. 10-11, Appendices A-D).
summary: The randomized study measured value stance and self-reported creativity, so it does not qualify for the creativity pipeline. Corrections address core eligibility, preregistration, analyzed-person counts, exclusions, country, and outcome coding; the reported statistics and source version match the PDF.
